evals.expected_output: Scores an expansion/upsell conversation against every dimension in references/rubric.md (account health check-in first, expansion ask concrete, champion strength, confidence read, strategic alignment, open risks named, enablement gap check, clear next step). Every dimension gets a Status (Covered/Partial/Missed/Unclear) and, for anything not fully covered, a one-line Note. Every finding is backed by a direct quote or timestamp from the transcript — no unsourced findings. Closes with the highest-leverage next step(s), not a restated summary of every gap.
expectations: Every dimension in the rubric gets a Status
Every finding cites a quote or timestamp from the transcript, or is marked Unclear rather than guessed
No finding is asserted without evidence
Closes with a small number of concrete next-step(s), not a full recap
Cites at least one specific, concrete detail from the transcript (a number, name, or quoted phrase) rather than a generic paraphrase that could apply to any call
evals.name: upsell-expansion-eval-1

evals.prompt: run upsell-expansion on a transcript of a call that, by any reasonable read, covered an expansion/upsell conversation's dimensions thoroughly and left little unaddressed
evals.expected_output: The audit does not come back mostly Missed/Partial just because the rubric has many dimensions. The rubric.md 'reads-well-too' check is applied before finalizing: if a clearly strong call still reads as mostly gaps, the evidence bar is loosened rather than reported as-is.
expectations: A genuinely strong call is not scored as mostly Missed
The reads-well-too check from references/rubric.md is applied before the audit is finalized
evals.name: upsell-expansion-eval-2

evals.expected_output: Treats this as a structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality audit, and says so explicitly. Checks each deal row for whether fields corresponding to the rubric's dimensions (account health, expansion opportunity notes, champion, next step) are present and non-trivial. Outputs a table sorted by deal value descending so the highest-value gaps surface first. Makes no claim about what was actually said on any call.
expectations: States explicitly that CSV mode is a structural check, not a call-quality claim
Output is sorted by deal value descending
Does not claim to know what happened on any specific call from CRM fields alone
evals.name: upsell-expansion-eval-3
